closed.title: Construct exact 29- and 106-product aggregation families and certify their cost scope
closed.body:
## Result

The cited Solomonik–Bläser examples (arXiv:2610.26563v2) aggregate 28 and 105 independent matrix products. This PR supplies explicit families of 29 and 106 products, complete correction budgets, and a uniform tensor identity.

Let x=n+1. Over every characteristic-zero field and every integer n >= 1:

| Independent products | Square matrix dimension | Exact rank upper bound |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 29 | n^3 | x^9 + 9x^8 + 36x^7 + 3x^6 |
| 106 | n^4 | x^12 + 12x^11 + 66x^10 + 139x^9 + 5x^8 |

The 29-product cost per output is strictly smaller than the cited 28-product budget for every n >= 1:
`29*r28 - 28*r29 = x^6*(x^3 + 9*x^2 + 7*x + 32) > 0`.

The 106-product cost per output is strictly smaller than the cited 105-product budget for every n >= 7:
`106*r105 - 105*r106 = x^8*(x^4 + 12*x^3 + 66*x^2 - 1451*x - 207)`.
At x=8+u, the quartic is `u^4 + 44*u^3 + 738*u^2 + 3957*u + 2649`. At n=6 the quartic is negative, so the threshold qualification is necessary.

The aggregation and correction method retain external credit. The new contributions are the exported families and their certified comparisons; no historical priority or optimality is claimed.

## Proof and exact certificates

Claims `AI-AGGREGATION-29-001` and `AI-AGGREGATION-106-002` are written and unreviewed.

A separate set-based checker covers all 24,389 mixed triples for 29 products and all 1,191,016 mixed triples for 106 products. Both have zero off-diagonal compatible triples. Complete correction families contain 48 and 222 subsets.

The proof uses rational centered dual embeddings and inclusion–exclusion. The finite certificates therefore give the full tensor identities for every positive n. External source files and ancillary examples are pinned by hashes.

Separate implementation controls evaluate all 159,651 rank-one positions at n=2 over F101 for the 29 family, and all 9,323,181 positions at n=2 over F2 for the 106 family. Each uses one complete scalar assignment; these are implementation checks, while the uniform proof supplies the all-coefficient result.

## Exact limitation relative to 9/4

Claim `AI-AGGREGATION-COST-FLOOR-003` proves that no balanced conflict-free family with N <= 10 can pass the direct 9/4 cost gate when it charges the full leading aggregate (n+1)^(3N) and nonnegative corrections.

Set C=binomial(3N,N), D=binomial(2N,N). The complete tripartition hypergraph has CD edges and degree D at every vertex. The selected p vertices in each of the three classes induce exactly p edges. Counting edges incident to the deleted vertices gives
`CD-p <= 3(C-p)D`, hence `p <= floor(2CD/(3D-1))`.

Weighted AM–GM and exact integer comparisons through N=11 give the exclusion through N=10. N>=11 is necessary only in this displayed-budget model; it is not sufficient. The result is not a tensor-rank lower bound and does not exclude cheaper aggregate decompositions.

## Validation

All 909 currently discovered test IDs have documented passing coverage:

- 895 unchanged cases retained from the complete 908-case construction receipt;
- the final 12-case aggregation module;
- two fresh claim-ledger and relative Markdown link checks after the final edits.

The receipt verifies source equivalence, exact disjoint replacement coverage, equality with current discovery, and evidence hashes. It explicitly records the interrupted prefix and subsequent shards; it does not claim one uninterrupted frozen-final-tree run.

All five historical archive replays passed. Failed bounded searches are archived with commands, seeds and limits; they are not nonexistence or optimality proofs.

Principal commands:
- `python research/ai/2026-10-23-aggregation-families/verify.py`
- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_aggregation_families.py -v`
- `python tools/replay.py`

Complete logs and receipts are in the package's `validation/` directory. The published final tree is `9d9a6948f114a2f7098921caae84ce0bd63a5d3f`, identical to local checkpoint `7792abb`.

## Review scope

The PR is ready for review; hosted CI remains pending and must pass before merging.

Neither family improves the matrix multiplication exponent. No restriction from the repository's polynomial source to these families is supplied. Owner-directed OpenAI Codex work; same-session checks are not independent mathematical review.

Related research from this round: #211 (Laurent cancellation) and #213 (two-sided A4 analysis).

closed.title: Extend paired-source channel barriers through Laurent cancellation and border substitution
closed.body:
## Result

The earlier paired-source channel barriers left singular Laurent cancellation open. This PR proves that the common low-channel-rank obstruction survives arbitrary poles in both the source and auxiliary contributions, provided the rank hypothesis holds over the full Laurent field.

Let V be a d-dimensional space of first-leg covectors on which the source contribution has generic channel rank at most rho < h, where h is the target inner width. If source plus a fixed auxiliary tensor R degenerates to M(l,h,r), then:

- the auxiliary first flattening has rank at least d;
- for d >= 1, the auxiliary border rank over C is at least `d+h-rho-1`.

The strengthened border-rank statement does not assert the same stronger bound for a flattening. Its proof uses substitution on first factors, primitive Laurent-vector normalization, and determinant specialization only after poles have cancelled. For border rank, a second approximation parameter is substituted as u=t^N with N greater than the total auxiliary-map pole budget. The proof states the field and formal-approximation qualifications explicitly.

## Paired-source consequence

For the stated finite-band/profile class, put
`gB=(r-m+1-2D-m*eB)_+`,
`gC=(l-m+1-2D-m*eC)_+`, and
`d0=(l*r-n^2+gB*gC)_+`.

The auxiliary first-flattening rank is at least d0. If d0 >= 1 and the common generic profile cap is rho < h, the auxiliary border rank is at least `d0+h-rho-1`.

At fixed widths, near-full outer dimensions and sublinear bandwidth/exception counts, the auxiliary cost is `n^2-o(n^2)`. Arbitrary first maps, arbitrary auxiliary maps, moving common channel bases and every finite pole order are allowed. Full generic channel rank, failure of the common factorization and macroscopic nonlocal regions remain outside this theorem.

## Evidence

Claims `AI-LAURENT-CHANNEL-SEPARATION-001`, `AI-LAURENT-PAIRED-REPAIR-002` and `AI-LAURENT-BORDER-MARGIN-003` are written and unreviewed. Proofs, standalone exact controls, source pins, claim ledger, status and research directions are included.

Five controls expand the complete native paired source with negative Laurent powers retained. Additional controls cover moving kernels, genuine pole cancellation, a raw constant-coefficient rank increase, rank-one channel encoding, sharp d=1 border-rank examples, and the strict N>P substitution condition.

## Validation and publication

- Complete 904-test coverage passed at substantive tree `799c5b8e07213790aa75db598a5bda0ee448fdcf`: 547 retained successes plus two disjoint remaining-ID shards of 179 and 178. The interrupted sequential process and exit130 are recorded; no completed test was repeated.

closed.title: Complete the projective conic normal-class lifting criterion
closed.body:
## Problem and result

The affine all-order conic theorem left the missing projective base points unclassified. This continuation proves that they introduce no additional component or hidden leading-rank exception.

For every complex base point
\[
([r:s],[a_0:a_1],[b_0:b_1])\in(\mathbb P^1)^3,
\]
the leading ranks remain 14,14,12. For a nonzero normal class \([\lambda:\mu]\), the existence of a second jet, a formal curve, and an exact polynomial curve are equivalent, with criterion
\[
(a_1r-a_0s)(b_1r+b_0s)(s\lambda^3+r\mu^3)=0.
\]

The first boundary velocity may be chosen. The theorem concerns existence for a normal class, not extension of every prescribed complete jet.

The solution set has exactly three irreducible components:
\[
[a_0:a_1]=[r:s],\qquad
[b_0:b_1]=[r:-s],\qquad
[r:s]=[\lambda^3:-\mu^3].
\]
This is a set-theoretic component statement.

## Evidence

- Rebuild the complete tangent and curvature operators on all three missing residual strata. Their tangent dimensions are 64+3+3, with 68 boundary directions and two normal directions. Each mixed curvature calculation has 49 unit pivots and an exact residual ideal.
- Check both pure normal classes separately, without inverting the mixed normal parameter.
- Verify literal source reversal on all 4,096 terms and its complete normal transition \([\lambda:\mu]\mapsto[\mu:\lambda]\). This supplies the conic chart at infinity.
- Export eight exact polynomial families and check all 29 possible product coefficients against an independent literal contraction, along with seven linear-component identities.
- Prove unit leading minors 1,1,-1 at every projective base point. The finite mixed families have degrees one and two in the curve parameter.

## Claims and attribution

Claim **AI-CONIC-PROJECTIVE-CRITERION-001** remains **proof-written-unreviewed**.

PR101 supplies the canonical source and complete affine obstruction; the earlier biform work supplies the common-factor projective base. PR136 supplies the affine all-order criterion and polynomial gauge construction. Eleven exact source pins preserve these inputs.

The prior affine claim retains its theorem and status. Its limitations field now explicitly identifies its affine scope and the new projective continuation. No frozen proof or operator is changed.

## Validation

All **7 focused mathematical tests pass**, with zero skips or failures. The producer suite completed in 55.648 seconds; a separate internal audit reran all seven in 49.801 seconds, including complete acceptance in 48.250 seconds.

The tests cover all projective strata, exact curves, source reversal, normal-coordinate transitions, source-pin and parser restrictions, incomplete degree data, incorrect residual generators, and allowed versus forbidden late perturbations.

All **9 repository/archive checks pass** after registration. All 11 pinned inputs, 17 frozen package files and 23 archived files match their approved originals byte-for-byte. The new branch is based on PR136 head 14c4da35 and contains main 3008d70.

The [frozen additive integration receipt](https://github.com/1337isnot1337/matrix-mult-bounds/blob/2344bec80f4cf15f31faf6f0ea3fb7690ed87c16/results/integration-2026-10-23-final/additive-pr167-projective/validation.json) passes at tested commit 19187753696e3f9d86daffdf78c01a168a1cf3b5: **26 new mathematical tests and 9 repository/archive checks**, zero skips or failures. Discovery finds **980 test IDs**, retaining all 954 previously validated IDs. The new package files match their frozen PR heads, and existing research/operator/test bytes and protected archives are unchanged. The receipt records the one intentional affine-claim limitations clarification. This reuses the full 924-test baseline, five historical replays and intervening additive gates; it is not a claim that all 980 tests were rerun together.

Current-head hosted CI and prerequisite merges remain merge gates.

## Dependency and scope

The result does not prescribe a full first or higher jet, change the fixed-third-jet obstruction in PR #156, or assert a scheme structure for the full incidence. It does not construct M(10,10,11) or improve the matrix multiplication exponent. Same-session AI auditing does not establish external mathematical review or formalization.

closed.title: Bound paired repair costs and certify residual-rank improvement criteria
closed.body:
## Problem and result

The paired polynomial-source program needs a precise distinction between the limits of its current formal operations and criteria for genuinely new tensor maps. This PR proves a repair-cost barrier inside the specified external formal calculus, proves the sharp coefficient over the complete external parameter family, and supplies exact finite and asymptotic criteria for an actual residual-repaired construction.

### Formal repair barrier

For fixed width `b>=2`, near-full outer dimensions require more than `O(n^alpha)` scalar repairs for every fixed `alpha<2` in the Amanov–van den Berg–Zuiddam formal preorder. Fixed outer defects require `liminf s_n log(n)/n^2 >= log(b^2/(2b-1))/e`. The coefficient is sharp over the whole external `F_theta` family, including boundary and corner parameter sequences. A uniform envelope also handles convergent logarithmic outer loss. These functions are not asserted to be actual tensor invariants; the result does not exclude arbitrary degenerations.

### Actual residual criteria

For a complex residual `E`, set `D=min(r_A*r_B,r_A*r_C,r_B*r_C)`. One genuine degeneration `Q(n,b) + E -> M(l,h,r)` would imply `omega<9/4` if `(l*h*r)^(3/4)>D^(3/4)+sqrt(2*b*(2*n+b-1)^3)/3`. The exact verifier identifies the smallest largest-source-leg format passing this full-target gate: 441, at `(n,b)=(21,8),(21,9)`.

A character-independent near-full family at fixed `b>=4`, with first residual rank `O(n^gamma)`, long ranks `O(n)`, and `gamma<1`, gives the quantified conditional bound in the proof. No maps satisfying an improvement criterion are supplied.

## Claims and sources

- `AI-OPERATIONAL-REPAIR-BARRIER-001`: written and unreviewed.
- `AI-RESIDUAL-RANK-FINITE-GATE-001` and `AI-RESIDUAL-RANK-ASYMPTOTIC-GATE-002`: conditional and unreviewed.
- Amanov, van den Berg and Zuiddam, arXiv:2610.30054v1, Definitions 5.3/5.5 and Proposition 5.9, with the formal-expression scope retained.
- Alman and Li, arXiv:2605.21738v1, Proposition 4.2 for compact matrix-spectrum attainment, with its prior attribution retained.
- Prior local paired-profile, correction-budget and endpoint arguments are pinned and credited in the package source records.

## Validation

closed.title: Construct three split border seeds and certify their grid constraints
closed.body:
## Result

This investigation starts from the externally credited AlphaTensor rank-76 M(4,5,5) decomposition, closes fruitless restricted searches, and constructs three explicit changed border seeds.

| Splits | Exact intermediate terms | Surviving border terms | Distinct U directions | Positive remainder coefficients |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Four | 80 | 76 | 72 | 51 |
| Five | 81 | 76 | 71 | 172 |
| Six with separate factor gauges | 82 | 76 | 70 | 73 |

Every witness includes exact factors and physical transformations. Complete rational Laurent contraction checks all 10,000 constant positions and every nonzero Laurent coefficient. The six-split witness succeeds under a condition that the earlier unscaled-arrow test cannot accept: each discarded tensor has positive valuation, while two individual factors have poles. Product-one factor gauges after epsilon=t^3 give an all-positive factor presentation. A nonzero mixed trace proves the distinction exactly.

## Grid consequences

The original seed's standard-flip component is closed. The four- and five-split seeds escape it, but exact component certificates prove that every finite standard-flip continuation of either still retains 50 W directions requiring at least ten rank-four groups. The specified Q(6,4) termwise evaluation grid has nine. A separate trace pairing also excludes further subset stabilizer deletion in the five-split component, including cancellation with the original discarded error.

The six-split seed has a different component: only 47 W directions are permanent. An exported rational cover places those 47 directions in nine rank-four groups; a matching integer-weight certificate proves that nine is the exact minimum. This PR covers only the permanent subset. Follow-up #154 supplies a scoped obstruction to fitting the six-split mobile factors and constructs larger seeds; it is kept separate from this accepted tree. closed.title: Exclude every A4 Laurent chart with one regular full-rank long leg
closed.body:

closed.title: Certify singular tensor constructions and sharp convolution packings
closed.body:
## Result and remaining exponent target

This PR develops actual tensor maps for the search below the arithmetic exponent 9/4. It now contains exact finite constructions through seven matched convolution sectors and all-size packing formulas. **It does not establish a smaller exponent or the unbounded family required by the growth criterion.** Written proofs and same-session replays are distinguished from external mathematical review and formalization.

## Canonical integer constructions

The new package `research/ai/2026-10-21-canonical-moment-flags/` gives literal integer maps, valid over every field:

| Target | Source | Full coefficient positions | Negative positions | Constant positions | Largest absolute map entry |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T4 | C(5,10) | 400 | 60 | 80 | 6 |
| T5 | C(6,16) | 1,125 | 175 | 175 | 1 |
| T6 | C(7,24) | 2,646 | 420 | 336 | 5 |
| T7 | C(8,34) | 5,488 | 882 | 588 | 2 |

All 9,659 positions were independently expanded with exact integer arithmetic. Every negative coefficient is zero; all constants are the required canonical target coefficients. The total is 195 target monomials. Frozen witness hashes and full positive remainders make the checks reproducible. The m6 replay caught and corrected an off-by-one error in the recovered moment list before acceptance.

The package contains separate constructors, a standard-library Python verifier, a standalone JavaScript replay, and tests for reconstruction, hashes, full coefficients, and two damaged-map controls. The restored local environment has now reconstructed and replayed all four Python certificates, including the stored hashes and damaged-map controls. The independent JavaScript replay also agrees.

These shorten the prior five-sector source from 20 to 16 and six-sector source from 28 to 24, while making all shared sector identifications agree. Claim: `AI-CANONICAL-INTEGER-FLAGS-001`.

## Free flags, all-size boundary pairs, and the affine continuation

- An exact 45-equation integral chart with an odd 45-by-45 Jacobian minor proves a complex C(7,15) degeneration to five independently based matched sectors. The proof verifies the central conic and explicit polynomial-kernel bases for the outer pencil. A separate literal F2 certificate checks all 1,125 source coefficients. The binary coefficients are not presented as complex coefficients. Claim: AI-FREE-ISOTROPIC-FLAGS-001.
- Explicit integer maps give C(m+2,m+1) to the two canonical boundary sectors C(2,m-1) and C(m-1,2) for every m>=3. An independent expansion checks 50,028 positions at m=3 through 20, and the all-size proof shows every basis determinant is a unit. This supplies two sectors, with the middle continuation still open. Claim: AI-BOUNDARY-PAIR-001.
- A scalar shifted-block theorem forces asymptotic source cost at least 3/2 under its full negative-moment hypotheses. Free quotient flags and affine carry rows are outside that class. Claim: AI-SCALAR-SHIFTED-BARRIER-001.
- An all-size affine six-row first flag has product dimension at most 3m+6, proved by three independent polynomial relation families. Its 142,653 integer relation checks and finite-field continuation are preserved. The complete C(9,23) six-sector witness is certified over F2 only. A stored 1,025-bit lift checks 540 congruences, but characteristic-zero existence remains unproved. Claims: AI-AFFINE-CARRY-FIRST-FLAG-001, AI-AFFINE-CARRY-M6-F2-002, AI-AFFINE-CARRY-LIFT-003.
